issue.body:
This PR stabilises `testILMDownsampleRollingRestart` and closes #136585. 

This test started failing more often after https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/135834 because this change increased the chance of manifesting https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/137422.

To reduce this chance we wait for ILM to finish the phase before we end the test.

Closes #136585

body:
It might look like we can fix this by moving the index name resolution step into the cluster state update since this would eliminate the gap in which the race occurs, but note that if security is enabled then we will already have performed index name resolution in `org.elasticsearch.xpack.security.authz.IndicesAndAliasesResolver#resolveIndicesAndAliases` so there'll still be a race.

Instead I think we need to adjust the cluster state update logic to treat "index doesn't exist" as an indicator of success and proceed with any other deletes in the batch, similar to this code here:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/569c1fc1cde793d943b1161e915727ec48d6ae25/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/action/admin/indices/delete/TransportDeleteIndexAction.java#L101-L102
I think we're seeing this in some other test failures too: https://es-delivery-stats.elastic.dev/app/r/s/NAduD. Those failures also seem to occur in the cleanup stage.

issue.body:
In some cases, an index may have already been deleted by the time we process the deletion cluster state update task. In that case, we can simply skip it instead of throwing an exception. Index name resolution will have failed in the transport action (or in security) if the index never existed.

Closes #137422
